text: ChatGPT doesn't know what it's going to say.
It guesses. One word at a time.
Your message is chopped into tokens, about three quarters of a word each.
Then it scores every token it knows, and asks one question: what comes next?
The cat sat on the... mat? 60 percent. Floor? 10. Moon? Almost zero.
It picks one, adds it to the sentence, and does it all again.
For every single token. Hundreds of times per answer.
Here's the part nobody tells you. It doesn't always pick the top one.
A setting called temperature adds a little randomness, so it doesn't sound like a robot.
That's why the same question can get a different answer every time.
Comment token, and I'll send you a free tool that shows how ChatGPT splits your words.
